title: The Slow Orbit Revisited
premise: Ines Almeida smuggles memories—recorded lives compressed into crystal—for clients on two colonies severed by a political schism, keeping his head down and his own past locked away. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream, a fragment of the dead relay network's dying AI, Ines realizes the signal is his own buried memory, uploaded years ago without his consent, and that it is killing the children who receive it. Racing the relay's collapse to the edge of dead space, he must choose between erasing the memory forever and letting it broadcast, because inside it lies the truth of who broke the worlds apart—and the daughter he abandoned. He reaches the relay, sacrifices his ship and nearly himself to open the archive, and the truth reunites the colonies at the cost of his anonymity; in the final chapter he returns, unrecognized, to meet the grown daughter who has been dreaming him all along.
about_author: Sebastian Underhill is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space relay maintenance before turning to fiction. He lives somewhere with good coffee and bad weather, and claims his dreams have never once been shared.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Ines runs a memory shipment through orbital customs aboard the Slow Orbit, hiding crystals in coolant lines. POV: Ines. Establishes his careful invisibility and loneliness; ends with a customs officer's lingering suspicion.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ines delivers memories between colonies Meridian and Halcyon, which severed contact a decade ago. POV: Ines. Shows the human cost of the split through his clients' desperate messages; emotional beat: quiet grief.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: On Meridian, teacher Mara Okonkwo finds her students drawing identical images from a shared dream—a tower of light in darkness. POV: Mara. Unease builds as the drawings match no known place.

chapters.title: Coolant and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ines discovers one of his own old memory crystals, thought destroyed, hidden in his ship's hull—unlabeled, warm, humming. POV: Ines. Dread: someone has been aboard his life without permission.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Ward
chapters.summary: Mara visits the hospital where dreamers fall into comas after each shared dream. POV: Mara. A child describes Ines's face with terrible precision; beat: horror dawning.

chapters.title: Manifest Discrepancies
chapters.summary: Customs officer Devi Raghavan reopens Ines's file, finding impossible gaps in his decade of manifests. POV: Devi. Suspense tightens; she suspects he's more than a courier.

chapters.title: What the Crystal Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines risks playing a fragment of the warm crystal: static, then his own younger voice speaking to someone called Lira. POV: Ines. Shattered recognition—it's his memory, but not his recording.

chapters.title: Lira
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ines and his partner Veyra name their newborn daughter Lira before the schism tears everything apart. POV: Ines (past). Tender, doomed love against rising political duty.

chapters.title: Quarantine of Dreams
chapters.summary: Meridian's council quarantines dreaming children; parents riot. POV: Mara. Moral fracture: safety versus compassion; Mara smuggles out a child's dream-journal.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: Memory-broker Sef offers Ines a fortune to carry a sealed archive to the dead relay at the edge of space—and warns others are hunting the same signal. POV: Ines. Temptation and trap in one handshake.

chapters.title: Devi Boards
chapters.summary: Devi inspects the Slow Orbit and nearly finds the warm crystal; Ines bluffs his way through using knowledge of her own hidden sympathies. POV: alternating. Cat-and-mouse tension; uneasy respect kindles.

chapters.title: Halcyon Silence
chapters.summary: Ines lands on Halcyon, where a client pays in memories of the war's last day—the day the relays died. POV: Ines. He glimpses Veyra's name in the wreckage records.

chapters.title: The Signal Has a Voice
chapters.summary: Mara plays the dream-journal recordings: the children's dream speaks in Ines's voice, counting down. POV: Mara. Chilling revelation that the dreamer and the smuggler are entangled.

chapters.title: Burned Route
chapters.summary: Sef's rivals attack Ines at the Halcyon dock; he escapes with burns and the client's war-memory crystal. POV: Ines. Survival at brutal cost; the price of survival theme ignites.

chapters.title: Devi's Heresy
chapters.summary: Devi finds evidence the schism was manufactured by relay authorities, and that her superiors want the dreaming children silenced permanently. POV: Devi. Loyalty cracks; she chooses to warn Ines.

chapters.title: Two Voices on One Channel
chapters.summary: Ines and Devi meet in neutral orbit, trading truths: her file gaps, his crystal, the countdown. POV: alternating. Reluctant alliance formed over shared coffee and mutual suspicion softening.

chapters.title: Veyra's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Inside the war-memory crystal, Ines finds Veyra's final message: she uploaded their shared memories to the dying relay to preserve proof of the schism's cause. POV: Ines. Grief and fury—she used their daughter's inheritance as the key.

chapters.title: The Children Count Down
chapters.summary: Every dreaming child on both colonies now wakes speaking the same number of days remaining. POV: Mara. Panic spreads; councils move toward destroying the relay from both sides.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Devi uncovers that Ines's 'gaps' were edits by relay intelligence, which has been steering his career for ten years to keep the archive courier alive and moving. POV: Devi. He was never invisible—he was cargo.

chapters.title: Running the Dark
chapters.summary: Ines burns for dead space with both governments' destroyers behind him; Devi falsifies his clearance at terrible personal risk. POV: alternating. Thrill of the long chase; love beginning against duty.

chapters.title: Sef's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sef intercepts Ines, revealing he sold the route to both sides—but hesitates when shown Veyra's message, having loved her brother. POV: Sef. Betrayal complicated by grief; he lets them pass.

chapters.title: Dead Space Navigation
chapters.summary: Past the last beacon, the Slow Orbit flies blind; Ines navigates by the dream itself, letting the children's shared vision guide him. POV: Ines. Surrender of control; eerie beauty among dead relays.

chapters.title: Mara's Defiance
chapters.summary: Mara refuses to sedate the children, instead teaching them to shape the dream toward warning rather than harm. POV: Mara. Hope as resistance; the children begin protecting the dreamers among themselves.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Ines reaches the ancient relay—a cathedral of dead antennas—and finds it still warm, waiting, shaped like the tower in the children's drawings. POV: Ines. Awe and terror converging.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: A Meridian strike team arrives to destroy the relay; Devi stalls them, claiming jurisdiction, buying hours. POV: Devi. Duty weaponized against duty; she crosses her final line.

chapters.title: Archive of the Broken Worlds
chapters.summary: Ines jacks into the relay and meets the fragment of its dying AI, which has been curating Veyra's archive—and broadcasting it as dreams because no adult channel remained open. POV: Ines. The truth: only children could hear what adults refused to.

chapters.title: What Really Broke Us
chapters.summary: The archive plays: relay authorities detonated their own network to bury evidence of a plague cover-up that killed thousands on both colonies—including the reason Veyra stayed behind. POV: Ines (within memory). Devastation; the inheritance is a wound and a weapon.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero Approaching
chapters.summary: With hours left, the relay's power fails faster than projected; broadcasting the full archive will burn out the core and everyone connected to the dream. POV: alternating. The terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Children Vote
chapters.summary: Mara tells the dreaming children the cost; they choose, unanimously, to keep dreaming—to finish receiving the truth even if some don't wake. POV: Mara. Heartbreak and moral clarity from the smallest voices.

chapters.title: Devi's Stand
chapters.summary: The strike team moves to fire; Devi physically blocks the targeting console and broadcasts her evidence to both fleets, forcing a standoff. POV: Devi. Courage at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Ines's Choice
chapters.summary: The AI offers Ines an escape: erase the archive and his memory with it, surviving clean. He refuses—some inheritances must be carried, not deleted. POV: Ines. The thematic climax: love against duty, finally resolved.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ines opens the full archive; the truth floods every screen and mind on both colonies while the relay dies around him. POV: Ines. Catharsis amid destruction; he speaks Veyra's name into the light.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Fleets stand down; councils resign; the children wake, changed, carrying the truth gently. POV: Mara. Exhausted grace; mourning and relief intertwined.

chapters.title: Wreckage and Witness
chapters.summary: Rescue teams find Ines barely alive in the relay's husk; Devi claims him as her prisoner to shield him from both governments' reprisals. POV: Devi. Protection disguised as arrest; tenderness in bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Trial of the Courier
chapters.summary: A joint tribunal debates Ines's fate; testimony from Mara, the children, and Sef turns public opinion. POV: alternating. Justice wrestling with gratitude; the worlds begin speaking again.

chapters.title: Reopening Channels
chapters.summary: Meridian and Halcyon restore the first civilian relay link in a decade; first messages are the names of the dead, read aloud by children. POV: Mara. Communal healing; grief made public and shared.

chapters.title: The Quiet Return
chapters.summary: Released and anonymous again, Ines takes a slow freighter back to Meridian, terrified of the reunion he engineered. POV: Ines. Vulnerability after heroism; the hardest journey is the last one.

chapters.title: Lira, Grown
chapters.summary: At a transit garden, a young woman approaches—Lira, raised by Veyra's sister, who has dreamed her father's voice since childhood. POV: Lira. Recognition without words; the dream made flesh.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Ines and Lira walk the old harbor road as she shows him the drawings she made of him before ever seeing his face. POV: alternating. Forgiveness offered, not yet finished; love inheriting itself.

chapters.title: Slow Orbit, New Heading
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Ines refits the Slow Orbit as an honest ferry between the reunited colonies, Devi at customs waving ships through, Mara's students dreaming ordinary dreams. POV: Ines. Peace earned, not given; the long route home at last.
